end.summary:
Practised grouping common animals by what they eat; the categories still need checking next time.
Built and read food chains with arrows, including a new chain; this was shown with a why/new-situation question.
Practised predicting changes when one living thing is removed; predictions were partly right and need more checking.
Practised that plants make their own food and begin food chains; this is still partly consistent.
The idea that only big animals are important was not corrected later in the lesson.
end.parentNote: Manav practised plant-eaters, meat-eaters, food-chain arrows, and what may change when one part of a chain is removed. Their method for reading arrow direction was shown clearly, and they also used sunlight to connect plants with making food; animal categories and removal predictions still need more checking. The mix-up that only big animals are important was not corrected later. At home, ask Manav to make one food chain and explain what might happen if one part is removed.
